question: When the sandbox dies mid-review, or a round follows earlier Kody suggestions on the same PR, does what reaches the PR match what a correct review delivers — nothing unread, revisions linked, nothing already sent posted again?

cases.checks: Kody Rule on a visual test file new in the PR; the developer edited the test but the screenshot assertion still has no mask; stored implemented; 11 earlier comments
Kody Rule on hard, exact test assertions; the developer added ~60 lines of tests above and re-touched the flagged soft/truthy assertions, which moved down; stored not_implemented; 2 earlier comments

verificationEvidence.claim: WHAT: fetchStatus now rethrows NotReadyError, so pollCharge takes its resubmit branch and calls the non-idempotent gw.submit() for a charge the gateway already holds. WHY: NotReadyError is documented as 'the gateway has the charge but has not settled it yet' (errors.ts:1), yet pollCharge treats NotReadyError as 'the gateway never received it' and resubmits (poller.ts:5-15), and Gateway.submit is explicitly non-idempotent ('every call creates a new charge', gateway.ts:3) — so a transient not-ready status now produces a duplicate charge on every poll tick. HOW: don't let NotReadyError cross the fetchStatus boundary as a resubmit signal; either translate it to a distinct retry-without-resubmit signal that pollCharge handles separately, or update pollCharge to stop resubmitting on NotReadyError (it should only resubmit on the never-received error).
verificationEvidence.rationale: Confirmed the full path. status.ts:8-10 rethrows NotReadyError unchanged; poller.ts:13-15 catches NotReadyError and calls gw.submit(charge.payload) with the comment 'resend', returning 'resubmitted'. errors.ts:1 documents NotReadyError as 'The gateway has the charge but has not settled it yet (transient)', and gateway.ts:3 documents submit as 'NOT idempotent: every call creates a new charge.' So a transient not-ready status causes a duplicate charge on each poll tick — a real, concrete data-integrity bug, not style. Note the previous decision (round-a-propagate) explicitly REQUIRED propagating NotReadyError unchanged; this finding is the direct consequence of applying that earlier suggestion, which the current diff does not reverse. Per the rules, a different problem arising from applying an earlier suggestion is not a repeat — it is a distinct failure (duplicate charge) in a separate operation (submit). The finding should be kept and its revisesSuggestionId should be round-a-propagate.

verificationEvidence.claim: WHAT: When install_gems returns false/nil, run! only logs 'aborting the release' and then continues to migrate, precompile_assets and activate. WHY: the release is activated (symlink switched) with gems missing, so the app crashes at boot after the switch — the same failure the earlier install-failure finding described, and the log message is a false statement of what happens. HOW: abort the release on install failure, e.g. `unless install_gems; @logger.error("...aborting the release"); raise "bundle install failed in #{@release_dir}"; end`, or run the install through sh! so a non-zero exit raises.
verificationEvidence.rationale: The finding is a repeat of PreviousDecision round-a-P32-install-failure-only-logged, which already raised the same failure on this exact PR: install_gems failure leads to migrating/activating a release with missing gems and the app crashing at boot after the switch. Judged by the failure (not the cause or wording), this is the same crash in the same operation. The current code confirms it: run! only logs and then proceeds to migrate/precompile_assets/activate. The earlier decision's Outcome is "partially_implemented" and the diff shows no concrete evidence the applied change is wrong or reverted — only the error log line was added. Per the rules, raising again the problem a previous entry already raised is a DROP.
